P4-A1.title: Engine phase 4: symmetries, folding, Euclidean geometry, Coxeter plane, Wythoff polytopes
P4-A1.summary: symmetries, fold with the orbit-sum rule, averagedRootsType and averagedSimpleCartan (the dual answer), symEig by cyclic Jacobi, euclideanBasis with E = Lambda^{1/2} V^T D^{1/2}, coxeterPlanePoints and coxeterPlaneRings with 6-decimal rounding and -0 as 0, coxeterWord, applyWordFloat, wythoffFaceTypes, wythoffFVector and wythoffEdges exactly; the golden tests of phase 4 and property 11.
spec: 2.17 (read only; the h4_projection test uses the exponents 1, 11, 19, 29)
5.5 (Eigenvectors; Type of the restricted or averaged roots)
oracle: classify_restricted (l.542; used by averaged types; ported in phase 6 by P6-A1: in phase 4 port the part needed and share the file src/satake.ts? No: put classifyRestricted in src/restrictedType.ts (plan) owned here, re-exported by satake.ts in phase 6)
owns: packages/engine/src/fold.ts, geometry.ts (phase-4 additions), wythoff.ts, restrictedType.ts (classifyRestricted, ported as it stands; plan), index.ts (exports)
deliverables: symmetries = relabellings(board, board) with the limit; fold: null folded with the reason when an orbit contains an edge, else A_fold[O'][O] = edges from O' into one fixed node of O; the folded board's labels in the Bourbaki order of the type identify names (CONTRACTS E-7 table) or orbit order when none
averagedRootsType by classifyRestricted on the averaged roots with the invariant form; averagedSimpleCartan = the transpose of the folded matrix where the board folds (test both)

symEig cyclic Jacobi, ascending eigenvalues; euclideanBasis E with E^T E = B; coxeterPlanePoints (rows for exponents 1 and h-1); coxeterPlaneRings with radii rounded to 6 decimals, -0 counted as 0, distinct_points, h_points_on_every_ring; coxeterWord (bipartite Coxeter element)
applyWordFloat: the same formulas on floats

wythoffFaceTypes: face types K with every component containing a ringed node; counts |W| / (|W_K| |W_K'|) as bigint; wythoffFVector; wythoffEdges by applying group elements to the base edges, with the cap

golden tests: every folding row (orbits, folds_to via identify, folded_cartan, folded_orbits_in_bourbaki_order, averaged_roots_type, averaged_simple_cartan, averaged_root_classes); every wythoff record (f_vector; edges where edges_enumerated; edge_length_squared where present as text); coxeter_plane rings for every type of rank 2 to 8 (sizes exact, radii within 1e-5), the coincident-points list; e8.h4_projection: the roots projected on the rows of E for exponents 1, 11, 19, 29 lie on two shells of 120 with radii in the ratio phi to five decimals
property 11: symmetric play commutes with folding in both games for every row with a folded board
acceptance: E8's 240 roots project to 8 rings of 30 and 240 distinct points; the Coxeter element rotates the plane by 2 pi / h (test)
traps: The factor Lambda^{1/2} is essential; bare eigenvectors distort the picture (2.14).
Eigenvector signs and repeated-eigenvalue bases are not unique: test invariants only (5.5).
For the rotation of D4 the folded matrix in the golden file is G2 with its nodes exchanged; compare in orbit order, and use folded_orbits_in_bourbaki_order for the drawn order (Appendix G).
A4's flip does not fold (an orbit contains an edge) but averages to BC2.
Face counts are bigint: 1_42 has 17280 vertices and 3628800 3-faces; |W(E8)| / |W_K| products exceed 2^31.

P4-A2.title: The projector and the build-time preset pipeline for T10
P4-A2.summary: draw/projector.ts: rotations in coordinate planes, orthogonal projection to two or three dimensions, a depth cue, Canvas 2D drawing of many edges, and the same code producing an SVG in Node for the build-time snapshot; the preset pipeline that computes the vertices and edges of every T10 configuration named in SPEC section 3 at build time and ships them as data files of at most 30 kB compressed.
spec: 7.1 (Drawing row: Canvas 2D, no library; the projector is our own code)
7.4 (SVG snapshot produced at build time by the same drawing code)
7.6 (E8 drawing under 100 ms; the drawing-time test)
3 M7 figure table (the configurations to precompute)
deliverables: projector.ts: rotation in any coordinate plane by angle; composition; orthogonal projection to the Coxeter plane or to three chosen coordinates; three turning angles about the horizontal, vertical and viewing axes (6.6 j parameter); depth cue by projected depth
canvasScene.ts drawing points and segments with the depth cue and the edge caps (70000 at rest; 8000 while turning); svgScene.ts producing the same picture as SVG in Node

presets.mjs run in prebuild: for every T10 configuration of section 3 (the default, root polytopes of A2, A3, D4, E8 showpiece, B3 face table, A2 two graphs, B3 make uniform, D4 Coxeter plane) compute vertices and edges with the engine and write JSON; a test fails if any file exceeds 30 kB gzipped
draw-time.spec.ts: the E8 root set with 6720 edges in the Coxeter plane draws in under 100 ms on the CI runner (measured with performance.now around the draw)
acceptance: every preset file at most 30 kB compressed (test)
projector round trip: rotating by theta then -theta is the identity to 1e-12; projection preserves the invariant form on the chosen plane (test)
traps: Preset files are fetched by the tool; no default state may need the worker (E-9).
The E8 edges are the 6720 pairs at inner product 1 (2.14); do not compute them by nearest-neighbour search in floats.

P4-A3.title: Tool T10 Geometry Studio
P4-A3.summary: Rings on nodes or the root polytope shortcut; the orbit as points in Euclidean coordinates; edges by the rule of 2.14; the face table; projections (flat, wireframe, orthogonal with Coxeter plane or three coordinates and rotations by buttons and keys as well as drag); the switch between polytope graph and move graph; make uniform in floating point; the E8 showpiece; the limits; presets from the build-time data; the SVG snapshot without JavaScript; every acceptance criterion of SPEC 4 T10 as tests.
deliverables: input: board and a non-negative integer per node (click to ring); root polytope shortcut ringing with numbers_of_highest_root and offering the short roots; output: points via euclideanBasis, edges via wythoffEdges, face table via wythoffFaceTypes; projections; the two-graph switch; make uniform (real start with a_i = c / sqrt(d_i) on ringed nodes, words replayed with applyWordFloat); showpiece E8 with 8 rings of 30; the statement of distinct dots when fewer than points; limits (70000 edges at rest, 8000 turning, vertices only above 70000 with a message; vertices up to 20000, else refuse with the orbit size); presets from the data files; enumerations above 2000 in the worker after the reader changes rings or board; SVG snapshot of the default projection without JavaScript

T10.test.ts: face counts equal f_vector for all 26 records; vertices and edges equal the first two f-vector entries where edges_enumerated; the root polytope in the Coxeter plane gives the golden ring sizes (radii to five decimals) and distinct_points; A2 from (1,1): the two graphs share four edges

T10.spec.ts: the showpiece loads from the preset file without the worker; rotation by keys; the B3 (0,1,1) make-uniform switch; the message above 70000 edges on a 2_41 configuration; the no-JavaScript SVG
acceptance: every bullet of SPEC 4 T10 acceptance has a passing test (G4)
traps: 'The root polytope' means the orbit of theta; short roots are a second set of points inside the hull (2.14).
On A3, A5, A7, B3, B6, D4 to D8, E6 roots coincide in the Coxeter plane; the tool must say the number of distinct dots (2.14).
Rotation must have button and key equivalents (A-8); any continuous rotation has a pause control and respects reduced motion (A-9).

P4-A4.title: Tool T11 Folding Bench
P4-A4.summary: Boards A2 to A8, D4 to D8, E6; big board and folded board side by side; the reader picks a symmetry; orbits coloured; symmetric play acting on a whole orbit with the folded board showing the same numbers; the folded board in Bourbaki order; the average tab naming the averaged type for every symmetry including the flip of A4; the golden tab arrives in phase 7; every acceptance criterion of SPEC 4 T11 as tests.
deliverables: the two boards; symmetry picker from symmetries(board); orbit colouring with labels; symmetric play; folded board drawn in folded_orbits_in_bourbaki_order; the average tab with averagedRootsType; the first tab's message when an orbit contains an edge; a slot for the golden tab (phase 7)

T11.test.ts: for every folding row with a folded board, 200 random symmetric plays agree between the two boards in both games and the folded board is folds_to; for every row the averaged type equals averaged_roots_type; for the flip of A4 the first tab reports that an orbit contains an edge
T11.spec.ts: A3 flip → B2; D4 rotation → G2; E6 → F4; the A5 average tab shows B3 and C3
acceptance: every bullet of SPEC 4 T11 acceptance has a passing test (G4)
traps: Two constructions, dual answers: name which one is shown (2.13).
The rotation of D4 has order 3: no quasi-split form; its folded matrix is G2 in orbit order with nodes exchanged relative to Bourbaki.
